correctness.rationale: Every five-tip rooted full binary topology is included; independently constructed exact symbolic variances prove both 1+4 shapes have V2<V3, and the 2+3 shape obeys exact polynomial gap identities. The explicit positive ultrametric witness has V2-V3=7/960 and V4-V3=1/1200. The minimum-tip bound uses V1=Vn=0 and the adjacency of the only two interior sample sizes at n=4. The final standalone checker passed all polynomial identities and independent exact enumeration of 31 subsets. No extension to arbitrary n or other sampling laws is assumed.

originality.rationale: The inspected 2012/2013 Nipperess–Matsen general moment formula supplies prior baseline but neither states the complete five-tip ultrametric root-topology dichotomy nor the two exact necessary-and-sufficient strict peak conditions. The article identifies shape sensitivity as further work. O'Dwyer et al. and Faller et al. use distinct sampling laws. Semantic searches of published findings and accessible historical claims did not reveal an equivalent exact classification. Structural originality is modest and specialized: the original general formula permits its variance data to be calculated; no independence of prior formulas is claimed.
residual_risks: Generic exact fixed-size phylogenetic variance formulas permit computational specialization, so determining whether the topology-phase characterization is independently original may require a domain specialist.
The PLOS supplemental PDF and complete Faller–Pardi–Steel article were not inspected. Published specialized tree-shape tables might be missed by semantic search.
The result has no demonstration that such multi-peaked variance is frequent in observed ecological trees.

value.rationale: Conditional phylogenetic rarefaction variance is a natural uncertainty statistic for biodiversity comparisons. Two distinct interior variance maxima invalidate a single-peak shape assumption already for a strictly positive ultrametric phylogeny with one mark per tip. The sharp topology dichotomy excludes all 1+4 shapes, and the exact two-polynomial region shows the effect is structurally stable rather than an arbitrary isolated numerical witness. It is not presented as an empirical prevalence estimate or as a new generic covariance formula.
